entry.name: if
entry.description: Evaluates input according to a conditional statement specified in an if-then-else form.

arguments.name: if
arguments.description: The arguments for theobject start with a conditional statement that uses the same syntax as. The wordfollows the conditional statement, which is then followed by a message expression. After the message expression, there is an optionaland a second message expression.evaluates the conditional expression, and if the result is non-zero, evaluates the message expression after the word. Otherwise, it evaluates the second message expression after the wordif anmessage is provided.

arguments.name: then, else
arguments.description: Message expressions are similar to what you type into abox.

arguments.name: $i1, $f1, $s1
arguments.description: You use,, orinstead offor replaceable arguments. The number of inlets is determined by how many different changeable arguments are typed in. The maximum number of inlets is 9.

arguments.name: send
arguments.description: No commas or semicolons are allowed. Messages can be sent to remoteobjects by preceding the message expression with, followed by the name of theobject.

arguments.name: out2
arguments.description: The keywordin a message expression creates a second, right outlet for theobject. Ifprecedes a message expression, the result of the expression is sent out the right outlet instead of the left outlet.

messages.name: bang
messages.description: In left inlet: Evaluates the conditional statement using the values currently stored.

messages.name: float
messages.digest: Replace a value and evaluate expression
messages.description: The number in each inlet will be stored in place of theorargument associated with it, and the expression will be evaluated.

messages.name: int
messages.digest: Replace a value and evaluate expression
messages.description: The number in each inlet will be stored in place of theorargument associated with it, and the expression will be evaluated.

messages.name: set
messages.description: The word, followed by one or more numbers, treats those numbers as if each had come in a different inlet, replacing the stored value with the new value, but the conditional statement is not evaluated and nothing is sent out the outlet. If there are fewer numbers in the message than there are inlets, the stored value in each remaining inlet is left unchanged.

messages.name: symbol
messages.digest: Replace a value and evaluate expression
messages.description: Symbols can only be received in the first inlet. If received in the first inlet, a symbol will be stored in place of theargument associated with it, and the expression will be evaluated, with the exception that you cannot do comparisons or use other operators with symbols. If the symbol shares the name of aobject, you can specify a position in the table to be evaluated.
